ConvertToLogSource.description:
Represents a conversion of a data source to a log source.

These conversions allow raw events from a given data_source to
be converted to a another 'compatible' log source. For instance,
this may be used to map:
Sysmon Event ID 1
to one of
[Windows Event Log Security 4688, Crowdstrike Process]

data_source.description: The data source to convert to a log source.
data_source.title: Data Source

mapping.description: The KEY represents the name of the field in this datasource. The VALUE represents the name of the filed in the target datasource.
mapping.title: Mapping

ConvertToLogSource.title: ConvertToLogSource

FieldMapping.description:
Represents a field mapping for a data source.

This object uses some overloaded terminology for legacy purposes
in the naming of the data_set vs data_model fields.

The "mapping" object, specifically, maps a field in the raw
data to a field in the target data_set.  For instance,
this can be used to convert a fields in a RAW data_source
to equivalent fields in CIM or OCSF.

data_set.description: The Common Information Model (CIM) datamodel that these fields in the mappings below map to.

data_model.description: The data mode for this mapping. This is used to determine how the data should be mapped.

mapping.description: The KEY represents the name of the field in this datasource. The VALUE represents the name of the filed in the target datasource.
mapping.title: Mapping

overloaded.  'data models' here are not the same as 'CIM Data Models'.
We anticipate that this naming may change as as certain DLX requirements
continue to evolve.

description:
Represents a DataSource object.

DataSources are highly specific, raw data that can power detections in ESCU.
They are far more specific than mapping to a specific Data Model.  For example,
an Endpoint.Processes mapping Data Model mapping does not account for whether
a detection only works on Windows, Linux, macOS, or another platform.  But a
DataSource mapping to 'Windows Sysmon EventID 1' for instance, is VERY specific
and gives high confidence of the EXACT data a detection should work against.

name.description: Each Security Content Object must have a unique name. Due to issues with how local/default stanzas are merged in the Splunk products, these names MUST NOT change between subsequent releases of content packs.
name.title: Name

id.description: Each Security Content Object must have a unique identifier. This is particularly important when leveraging many of the Content Versioning features built into Enterprise Security 8+. Unique ids may be generated with a python command such as `uuid.uuid4()` or similar.
id.title: Id

version.description:
The version of this object. This number MUST be incremented in the following circumstances:
1. Any time the object in this file is modified
2. Any time that the serialization logic for this object changes, changing what is written in its conf file stanza(s)
3. Any time that an object this object references, for example via enrichment, causes a change in its associated conf file stanzas(s).
This final determination is challenging to make manually, so the `contentctl inspect command` will help identify when this a version increment is required.
version.title: Version

creation_date.description: The date that this object was created. This should NEVER be updated.
creation_date.title: Creation Date

modification_date.description: The date that this object was last modified. This should be updated whenever the object is modified.
modification_date.title: Modification Date

author.description: The author of this object. This is a freeform string that can be used to identify the author of the object. It will eventually be replaced by a more detailed Contributors list.
author.title: Author

description.description: A description of the Security Content Object. This should be a human-readable description of the object, including its purpose.
description.title: Description

references.description: A list of references to external resources that are relevant to this object. This can include links to documentation, blog posts, or other resources that provide additional context or information about the object.
references.title: References

mitre_components.description: The list of MITRE components that this data is related to.
mitre_components.title: Mitre Components

source.description: The Splunk 'source' field for this data.
source.title: Source

sourcetype.description: The Splunk 'sourcetype' field for this data.
sourcetype.title: Sourcetype

separator.description: The separator used to parse the data.
separator.title: Separator

supported_TA.description: The list of Splunk TA(s) that can parse this data. It is STRONGLY suggested to include at least 1 TA here, however some raw data does not have a supporting TA to parse it. In that case, it is acceptable not to populate this list.
supported_TA.title: Supported Ta

fields.description: The list of fields in this data. While populating this list is STRONGLY suggested, it is not required.
fields.title: Fields

field_mappings.description: The list of mappings from this type of data to another type of data such as cim or OCSF.
field_mappings.title: Field Mappings

example_log.description: An example log for this data. This is helpful, additional documentation so that users can immedaitely understand what the raw data looks like.
example_log.title: Example Log
